---
title: "Glossary"
subtitle: "Plain-English definitions of the terms used across this site."
---

If a word on another page is unfamiliar, it's probably here. Definitions are
written for an economist, not a software engineer.

## Agentic AI

**Agentic coding** — giving an AI direct access to your project files so it
can read them, edit them, and run code on your behalf, under your
supervision. Contrasted with chatting in a browser, where you copy and paste
by hand. See [What is agentic coding?](big-picture/what-is-agentic.qmd).

**Agent** — the AI working on your behalf. Claude Code is an agent.

**Prompt** — what you type to the AI: your instruction or question.

**Plan mode** — a Claude Code setting where it reads the relevant files and
writes out a plan *before* changing anything. You turn it on with
`Shift+Tab`. Read the plan and suggest edits or missing detail before you
approve it, rather than rubber-stamping it. Good for multi-file changes.

**Tool call** — an action the agent takes, shown to you as it works: reading
a file, running a command, editing a file. You'll see labels like `Read`,
`Bash`, or `Edit`.

**Hallucination** — when the model states something false with full
confidence — a made-up citation, a regression number it didn't actually
compute. See [Hallucinations](pitfalls/hallucinations.qmd).

**Skill** — a reusable instruction set you can invoke by name (`/name`), so
you don't retype a multi-step request. See [Building your own
skills](workflow/building-skills.qmd).

**`CLAUDE.md`** — a plain-text file in your project that Claude reads at the
start of every session, holding project-specific notes (software versions,
conventions, what's off-limits).

**Context window** — how much text the model can consider at once. A large
one is why an agent can read a whole replication package or paper.

## Git and version control

**Git** — a tool that takes snapshots of your project so you can review
changes and undo them. See the [Git page](getting-started/git.qmd).

**Repository (repo)** — a folder that Git is tracking.

**Commit** — one saved snapshot, with a short message describing it.

**Diff** — the exact before/after lines a change touched. "Read the diff"
means look at precisely what changed before accepting it.

**Branch** — a parallel line of work you can develop and then merge back.

**Merge / merge conflict** — combining two lines of work; a *conflict* is
when both edited the same line and Git asks you to choose.

**Hash** — a commit's short ID, like `8dad523`.

**HEAD** — Git's name for the commit you're currently on.

**Staging** — marking which changes go into the next commit (`git add`).

**Remote / push / pull** — a copy of the repo hosted elsewhere (e.g.
GitHub); *push* sends your commits there, *pull* fetches others'.

**Clone** — download a copy of a remote repository.

**Worktree** — a second working folder backed by the same repository, on its
own branch — useful for working on two versions at once.

**`.gitignore`** — a file listing things Git should not track (build
artifacts, large data, secrets).

## Terminal and files

**Terminal** — the text window where you type commands. See the [terminal
primer](getting-started/terminal-and-bash.qmd).

**Shell (bash, zsh)** — the program inside the terminal that runs your
commands. `zsh` is the Mac default; `bash` is near-identical for our
purposes.

**CLI (command-line interface)** — using a program by typing commands rather
than clicking. Claude Code is a CLI tool.

**IDE** — an integrated development environment: a code editor with extra
tooling built in. VS Code and RStudio are examples.

**Flag / argument** — extras after a command: a *flag* is an option
(`--vanilla`), an *argument* is what you act on (`analysis.R`).

**Path** — a file's address. *Absolute* starts from the disk root
(`/Users/you/…`); *relative* starts from where you are (`data/raw.dta`).

**Symlink** — a shortcut that points one location at another.

**Recursive** — applied to a folder and everything inside it.

**Wildcard** — a pattern like `*.do` meaning "every file ending in `.do`".

## Tooling

**Orchestrator / master script** — one script that runs every step of a
project in order (clean → estimate → tables → compile).

**Makefile** — a script that re-runs only the steps affected by a change;
useful for slow pipelines.

**Lockfile** — a file recording the exact package versions a project used,
so it reproduces elsewhere. Examples: R's `renv.lock`, Julia's
`Manifest.toml`.

**Dependencies** — the external packages your code needs to run.

**Build artifacts** — files produced by running things (`.aux`, `.log`,
compiled output) that you don't keep in version control.

**Node.js / npm** — the runtime and package installer used to install Claude
Code (a one-time setup step).

**WSL** — Windows Subsystem for Linux: a way to run a Linux terminal on
Windows.
